clue.text: Husband finding one's bra size a bit of a problem

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a C cup is one of the standard bra sizes

explanation.surface: A husband discovers his partner's bra size and finds it something of a worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor setback or snag, so it is a small trouble.

clue.text: Knock cap off sleeping policeman

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so taking it off removes the first letter of the word for knock

parts.note: to knock is to thump

explanation.surface: An instruction to knock the top off a traffic-calming bump in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping policeman is the British name for a speed bump across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed hump is the raised ridge in a road that British drivers call a sleeping policeman.

clue.text: Nazi con involved it

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A Nazi swindle was mixed up in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun but is the old bar name for Italian vermouth, as in 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is short for Italian vermouth, and Cinzano is a well-known brand of that drink.

clue.text: Union forcing rebellion

parts.note: prising means forcing something open with a lever

explanation.surface: A trade union pushes its members toward a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a revolt by people against those in power, a synonym for rebellion.

clue.text: Plods are unexpectedly fast runners

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Slow-moving police officers turn out, against expectation, to be quick on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOD is British slang for the police, which makes the speed sound surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Big cats of this kind can sprint very quickly, so they are an example of animals that run fast.

clue.text: Non-stop bile, not decently articulable

parts.note: an express train runs non-stop between stations

indicators.note: doing something indecently means doing it improperly, so the word bile is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone spews bile without pause, in words too rude to be said.
explanation.definitionFit: Something articulable can be put into words, which is what capable of being expressed means.

clue.text: Woman in department retired in a huff

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in puts the woman's name inside the abbreviation for department

parts.note: DEP is an abbreviation for department
Eve, the first woman, stands for any woman in crosswords

explanation.surface: A woman in an office department walks off sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: Being peeved means being annoyed and sulky, the same mood as being in a huff.

clue.text: Showing many facets of Sue, unclothed

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters of the legal word go

parts.note: to sue someone is to prosecute them in court

explanation.surface: A portrait of a naked woman named Sue reveals many sides of her.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb meaning take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose-cut gem is faceted all over its domed top, so it shows many small faces.

clue.text: Proper wicked hash pipes!

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters are behaving badly and so end up rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims with delight over some excellent cannabis pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, which is proper in the sense of correct and tidy.

clue.text: Bloke initially unsure about fertility treatment

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: initially means taking only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, used to mean about

explanation.surface: A man who is uncertain at first about undergoing fertility therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fertility treatment' suggests IVF, but here it is something spread on fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure is dung spread on soil to make it fertile, a treatment for the land rather than people.

clue.text: Media bores like endless socialising at Davos, for example

indicators.note: bores means drills into, so the word for the media goes inside the other piece
endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: akin means similar to, or like
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: The journalists find the social whirl of the Davos summit tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Davos is both the venue of the World Economic Forum and a Swiss ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the drinking and partying that follows a day on the slopes at a ski resort such as Davos.

clue.text: Pen secret deception?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer's first word is an anagram signal and its second word gives the rearranged letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A request to write down a secret lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining goods by deceit is the legal offence of deception, misrepresenting oneself to gain money.

clue.text: Using depilator on or near a canine?

indicators.note: using the letters means putting them to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about whether to put hair remover on a dog, or near it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog, but it is a tooth, and the answer means around the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodontal describes the tissues around a tooth, and a canine is one of the teeth.

clue.text: Promises no unfair wordplay

indicators.note: unfair means not straight, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Someone vows there will be no cheating word games.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping the starting sounds of two words is a well-known kind of verbal joke, so it is wordplay.

clue.text: Sauna without a massage causing overheating

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the sauna word loses its letters a

parts.note: a stroke is a gentle rubbing movement of a massage

explanation.surface: A sauna followed by no massage leaves someone dangerously hot.
explanation.walkthrough: Both of the letters a in the word for the steam room are dropped, leaving SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatstroke from too much sun is a dangerous overheating of the body.

clue.text: Beating odds to fly a Spitfire

indicators.note: letting the odd-numbered letters fly away leaves just the even ones of the word

explanation.surface: A wager that a wartime fighter plane will win against the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitfire' suggests the RAF fighter plane, but it is a volcano spitting fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna in Sicily is an active volcano, which spits out fire and lava.

clue.text: It goes round the neck of a dog

parts.note: a Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Something that circles a dog's neck, such as a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: This wide cravat is worn knotted around the throat, so it is neckwear.

clue.text: Appoint celebrity underwriter

definitions.meaning: to ... someone to a post is to appoint them
at Lloyd's of London, an individual backer who underwrites insurance is called a ...

explanation.surface: An instruction to appoint a famous person to underwrite something.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: to nominate, a famous figure, and the Lloyd's of London term for an individual insurance backer.

clue.text: Sweet Manx language

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Malteser is a British chocolate sweet with a malted honeycomb centre

explanation.surface: A sweet called Manx language, as if the Isle of Man's tongue were a confection.
explanation.walkthrough: Maltesers are a British chocolate-covered malt ball sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Maltese is the national language of Malta, a Semitic tongue written in Latin letters.

clue.text: Capable of igniting committee shattered by massive service cut

parts.note: bust means broken or shattered

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the church service word is taken out of the next word

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A committee is broken up by heavy cuts to public services.
explanation.definitionFit: Combustive things burn readily, so they are able to catch fire.

clue.text: Whole of Bury, say, is quarantined

indicators.note: quarantined means kept shut away inside, so the example goes inside the word for bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: The whole of the town of Bury is put into quarantine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number is one without fractions, which is what this mathematical term means.

clue.text: Most likely asleep after disheartening match

indicators.note: after puts the first piece ahead of the match word
disheartening means removing the heart, leaving only the outer letters of the word

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A spectator dozes off after a depressing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptest is the superlative of apt, meaning most inclined or most likely to happen.

clue.text: Kent changing cubicle

parts.note: Clark Kent, the alter ego of Superman, famously changes his clothes in a street call box

explanation.surface: A changing room in the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent looks like the English county, but it is Clark Kent of the Superman stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A public call box was where Superman's mild alter ego swapped into his costume.

clue.text: Runs into road, showing caution

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside the road word

parts.note: a way is a road
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs into the road, which is a warning to be careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary means being careful and on guard, which is showing caution.

clue.text: Loathsome letters about Arnold Bennett?

indicators.note: about here means the answer lies around inside the run of those two words

explanation.surface: Someone writes hateful letters about the novelist Arnold Bennett.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett was an English novelist; an omelette named after him, with smoked haddock and cheese, was created at the Savoy hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette Arnold Bennett is a classic Savoy dish made with smoked haddock, so the novelist's name is an example.

clue.text: Shame of Top Gear star's mum

parts.note: The Stig is the anonymous racing driver on the BBC motoring show Top Gear
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: The embarrassment of a television motoring personality's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone, so it is a form of shame.

clue.text: Able to stand elite poncing about round playing field?

indicators.note: round puts the jumbled letters around the playing-field word
poncing about means fooling around showily, so the letters of elite are jumbled

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, British slang for a public playing field

explanation.surface: Upper-class people preening around a sports ground, ready to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: Erectile describes tissue that can become rigid and upright, so it is able to stand.

clue.text: Dictator's too wise to entertain toff on a regular basis

indicators.note: to entertain means to host inside, so the nobleman goes between the two letters
a dictator here is someone dictating words to be heard, so the next phrase is what is said

parts.note: said out loud, this sounds like two letter Ys
an earl is an aristocrat, a toff

explanation.surface: A dictator is too clever to host a toff.
explanation.walkthrough: Dictator is a person speaking for someone to write down, not a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yearly happens once each year, at a regular interval.
